source_text:
μήσομεν. Ἑορτάσει δὲ σὺν ὑμῖν κατὰ τὸν ἴσον νόμον, καὶ συνησθήσεται χαίρουσιν ὁ προσήλυτος. Τοὺς γάρ τοι κατὰ καιροὺς τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ πίστεως προσιεμένους τὰ αὐχήματα, ποιούμεθα κοινωνοὺς τῆς ἀναιμάκτου θυσίας, καὶ τῆς ἁγίας τραπέζης καλοῦμεν εἰς μέθεξιν. Κἀκεῖνο δὲ οἶμαι προσεπενεγκεῖν ἀναγκαῖον, ὅτι κεκράτηκεν ἔθος ἐν Ἐκκλησίαις, ἀπό γε, οἶμαι, τοῦδε τοῦ νόμου, ὡς εἰ ἐκπίπτοι τοῦ πρώτου μηνὸς, ἡ κατὰ σελήνην τεσσαρεσκαιδεκάτη, τὸν δεύτερον καὶ ἀγχοῦ περιεργάζεσθαι μῆνα, καὶ ἐν αὐτῷ ζητεῖν τὴν ὡρισμένην ἡμέραν, ἵνα μὴ ἐξοίχοιτο τοῦ ἀληθοῦς τῆς ἑορτῆς ὁ καιρός. Ἔχει δὲ οὕτω τὸ χρῆμα, καθὰ καὶ τῷ πάλαι προηγόρευται νόμῳ.
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Ὀρθῶς ἔφης· πλὴν, ἐκεῖνο φράσον. Εἰ μὴ παντί τῳ τυχὸν καὶ εἰ ἐν ὁδῷ γένηται μακρᾷ, καὶ ὡς ἀπωτάτω τῆς Ἱερουσαλὴμ, ἐφῆκεν ὁ νόμος ἀνεπιλήπτως δύνασθαι τὸ Πάσχα πληροῦν.
{ΚΥΡ.} Οὐ μὲν οὖν· ἐν μόνῃ γὰρ δὴ καταθύειν ἐκέλευε τῇ ἁγίᾳ πόλει, ἐν ᾗ καὶ τὸν πάλαι ναὸν ὁ Σολομὼν ἀνεδείματο. Προσεφώνει δὲ οὕτως ὁ Μωσῆς ἐν τῷ Δευτερονομίῳ τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραὴλ, λέγων· «Φύλαξαι τὸν μῆνα τῶν νέων, καὶ ποιήσεις τὸ Πάσχα Κυρίῳ τῷ Θεῷ σου, ὅτι ἐν τῷ μηνὶ τῶν νέων ἐξῆλθες ἐξ Αἰγύπτου νυκτός. Καὶ θύσεις τὸ Πάσχα Κυρίῳ τῷ Θεῷ σου, πρόβατα καὶ βόας ἐν τῷ τόπῳ ᾧ ἐὰν ἐκλέξηται Κύριος ὁ Θεός σου αὐτὸν, ἐπικληθῆναι τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ἐκεῖ. Οὐ φάγῃ ἐπ' αὐτοῦ ζύμην. Ἐπτὰ ἡμέρας φάγῃ ἐπ' αὐτοῦ ἄζυμα, ἄρτον κακώσεως, ὅτι ἐν σπουδῇ ἐξήλθετε ἐξ Αἰγύπτου, ἵνα μνησθῆτε τὴν ἡμέραν τῆς ἐξοδίας ὑμῶν ἐκ γῆς Αἰγύπτου πάσας τὰς ἡμέρας τῆς ζωῆς ὑμῶν. Οὐκ ὀφθήσεταί σοι ζύμη ἐν πᾶσι τοῖς ὁρίοις σου ἑπτὰ ἡμέρας, καὶ οὐ κοιμηθήσεται ἀπὸ τῶν κρεῶν ὧν ἐὰν θύσητε τὸ ἑσπέρας τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ πρώτῃ εἰς τὸ πρωΐ. Οὐ δυνήσῃ θῦσαι τὸ Πάσχα ἐν οὐδεμιᾷ τῶν πόλεών σου ὧν Κύριος ὁ Θεός σου δίδωσί σοι, ἀλλ' ἢ εἰς τὸν τόπον ὃν ἂν ἐκλέξηται Κύριος ὁ Θεός σου, ἐπικληθῆναι τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ἐκεῖ. Θύσεις τὸ Πάσχα ἑσπέρας πρὸς δυσμὰς ἡλίου ἐν τῷ καιρῷ ᾧ ἐξῆλθες ἐξ Αἰγύπτου, καὶ ἑψήσεις καὶ ὀπτήσεις καὶ φάγῃ ἐν τῷ τόπῳ, ᾧ ἐὰν ἐκλέξηται Κύριος ὁ Θεός σου αὐτόν.» Μυρίαις μὲν γὰρ ὅσαις πόλεσί τε καὶ κώμαις ἡ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἐπεπλήθη χώρα, τελεῖν δὲ καὶ τὰ ἱερὰ καὶ τὸν ἐπὶ τῷ Πάσχα νόμον, ἐν μόνῃ δὲ χρῆναι τῇ ἁγίᾳ πόλει διετύπου Θεὸς, ἐκεῖνο, οἶμαί που, σκιαγραφοῦντος ἡμῖν εὖ μάλα τοῦ νομικοῦ γράμματος, ὡς οὐκ ἂν εἴη θέμις οὔτε μὴν ἐφεῖταί τισι τὸ ἐπὶ Χριστῷ μυστήριον, καθ' ὃν ἂν ἕλοιτο τρόπον, ἤγουν ἐν τόπῳ παντὶ δύνασθαι πληροῦν· χῶρος γὰρ μόνος ὁ πρέπων αὐτῷ, καὶ οἰκειότατος ἀληθῶς, ἡ ἁγία πόλις, τουτέστιν, ἡ Ἐκκλησία, ἐν ᾗ καὶ νόμιμος ἱερεὺς, καὶ διὰ χειρῶν ἡγιασμένων τελεῖται τὰ ἱερὰ, καὶ θυμίαμα προσφέρεται τῷ πάντων κρατοῦντι Θεῷ, καὶ θυσία καθαρὰ, κατὰ τὴν τοῦ προφήτου φωνήν. Δι' οὐδενὸς οὖν ἄρα τὸν ἐπὶ τῷδε ποιοῦνται
pass_a_gloss: (we will hon)or. And the proselyte will feast with you according to the equal law, and will rejoice with (you) rejoicing. For those who in seasons accept the boasts of the faith in Christ, we make sharers of the bloodless sacrifice, and we call to participation of the holy table. And I think it necessary to add that also: that a custom has prevailed in Churches, from this law, I think, that if the fourteenth according to the moon falls out of the first month, to busy oneself with the second and near month, and in it to seek the defined day, so that the season of the feast might not depart from the truth. And the matter holds thus, just as also was proclaimed beforehand to the ancient law. PALLADIUS: You said rightly; but tell that: whether the law did not perhaps allow to anyone, even if he should be in a long road and as farthest from Jerusalem, to be able to fulfill the Passover blamelessly. CYRIL: Not indeed; for it commanded to sacrifice in the holy city alone, in which also Solomon built the ancient temple. And Moses addressed thus in Deuteronomy the sons of Israel, saying: Guard the month of the new (things), and you will make the Passover to the Lord your God, because in the month of the new things you went out of Egypt by night. And you will sacrifice the Passover to the Lord your God, sheep and oxen, in the place which the Lord your God chooses it, for his name to be invoked there. You will not eat leaven upon it. Seven days you will eat upon it unleavened (breads), bread of hardship, because in haste you went out of Egypt, so that you may remember the day of your exodus from the land of Egypt all the days of your life. Leaven will not be seen for you in all your borders seven days, and there will not sleep (remain) from the meats which you sacrifice in the evening on the first day until the morning. You will not be able to sacrifice the Passover in any one of your cities which the Lord your God gives you, but only into the place which the Lord your God chooses, for his name to be invoked there. You will sacrifice the Passover in the evening toward the setting of the sun, at the season in which you went out of Egypt, and you will boil and roast and eat in the place which the Lord your God chooses it. For with countless many cities and villages the land of the Jews was filled, but God prescribed that the sacred things and the law of the Passover must be completed in the holy city alone, the legal letter shadow-drawing very well for us this, I think somewhere: that it would not be right, nor indeed is it permitted to some, to be able to fulfill the mystery about Christ in whatever way he might choose, or in every place; for the only place fitting to it and truly most proper is the holy city, that is the Church, in which there is also a lawful priest, and through sanctified hands the sacred things are completed, and incense is brought to the God ruling all, and a pure sacrifice, according to the voice of the prophet. Through nothing then do they make the (law) about this (continues).
pass_b_english: Cyril: … And the proselyte will keep the feast with you under the same law and will share the joy of those who rejoice. For those who at the right times accept the glories of faith in Christ we make partners in the bloodless sacrifice, and we call them to share in the holy table. And I think it necessary to add this as well: a custom has prevailed in the churches, taken, I think, from this very law, that if the fourteenth day of the moon falls outside the first month, the second month, the one next to it, is examined, and the appointed day is sought in it, so that the true season of the feast may not slip away. That is how the matter stands, just as it was laid down beforehand in the ancient law.

Palladius: You have spoken rightly. But tell me this. Did the law perhaps allow anyone at all, even if he were on a long journey and as far as possible from Jerusalem, to keep the Passover without blame?

Cyril: Certainly not. It commanded the sacrifice to be made only in the holy city, the city in which Solomon also built the ancient temple. Moses addressed the sons of Israel in Deuteronomy as follows: ‘Observe the month of the new crops, and you shall keep the Passover to the Lord your God, because in the month of the new crops you came out of Egypt by night. And you shall sacrifice the Passover to the Lord your God, sheep and oxen, in the place which the Lord your God chooses, for his name to be called upon there. You shall not eat leaven with it. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread with it, the bread of affliction, because you came out of Egypt in haste, so that you may remember the day of your departure from the land of Egypt all the days of your life. No leaven shall be seen with you in all your borders for seven days, and none of the meat which you sacrifice in the evening on the first day shall be left overnight until morning. You may not sacrifice the Passover in any of your cities which the Lord your God gives you, but only at the place which the Lord your God chooses, for his name to be called upon there. You shall sacrifice the Passover in the evening, at the setting of the sun, at the time when you came out of Egypt; and you shall boil and roast and eat it in the place which the Lord your God chooses’ (Deuteronomy 16:1–7).

The land of the Jews was filled with countless cities and villages, yet God prescribed that the sacred rites and the law of the Passover must be fulfilled in the holy city alone. In this, I think, the letter of the law sketches very well for us that it would not be right, nor is it allowed to anyone, to fulfill the mystery of Christ in whatever way he pleases, or in any place at all. For the only place fitting for it, and truly most proper to it, is the holy city, that is, the Church, in which there is a lawful priest, and the sacred rites are performed by sanctified hands, and incense is offered to God who rules over all, and a pure sacrifice, as the prophet’s voice says (Malachi 1:11). So in no way do they keep the …

choices.english: the month of the new crops
choices.why: LXX ‘month of the new things’ (Hebrew Abib); Cyril explains it in §16 as the season when the new produce is gathered.
Palladius asks a question; Cyril answers ‘Certainly not’ (Οὐ μὲν οὖν).

choices.english: So in no way do they keep the … (law, §14)
choices.why: The sentence runs across the column break; its subject (the heretics) and ‘law’ stand at the start of §14.
